| P36 | Shared cloud authentication, asynchronous query jobs and query-cost budget contracts | P10, P25, P32 | No model-supplied destinations/credentials; expired auth, polling/cancel, billing estimates vs enforceable limits distinguished |
| P37 | BigQuery | P36 | Dataset/table scopes, dry-run/maximum billed-byte controls, typed results, job cancellation and polling budgets |
| P38 | Snowflake | P36 | Role/database/schema/warehouse scope, supported key/OAuth flows, time/resource controls, exact types and native cancellation; no invented hard dollar cap |
| P39 | Databricks SQL | P36 | Warehouse/catalog/schema scope, statement job limits, cancellation and bounded result-link downloads to approved destinations |
| P40 | Redshift | P11, P36 | Reuse PostgreSQL transport where valid; independently test IAM, catalogs, types, query limits and cancellation |
| P41 | Trino | P36 | Catalog/schema policies, next-page URI validation, bounded polling/results and native cancellation |
| P42 | Elasticsearch/OpenSearch | P25, P32 | Index/alias restrictions, typed read DSL, bounded pagination, partial/time-out reporting and no administrative passthrough; test both products |
| P43 | DynamoDB | P36 | IAM/table/index restrictions, bounded reads and consumed-capacity accounting, pagination; unrestricted scans disabled by default |
| P44 | Cassandra/ScyllaDB | P25 | Keyspace/table scope, bounded paging/partition reads, exact types and timeouts; no unbudgeted filtering/cluster scan; test both products |
| P45 | Db2 | P06 feasibility, P25 | Maintained driver or explicit vendor/ODBC dependency, platform/license/size disclosure, exact values, native permission and cancellation tests |
| P46 | Neo4j | P25, P32 | Graph/database scope, read transaction/account, procedure restrictions, exact graph values, bounded traversal/output and cancellation |
| P47 | Qdrant | P25, P32 | Collection-scoped typed vector/search reads, filter/point/payload budgets and exact metadata; no administrative passthrough |
| P48 | Milvus | P25, P32 | Database/collection/partition scope, bounded typed search/query, scalar/vector fidelity and job cancellation |
| P49 | Weaviate | P25, P32 | Collection/tenant isolation, typed bounded search, configured module behavior and no destination/credential override |
| P50 | Hosted/protocol-compatible service certification and full feature matrix | Relevant adapters | Explicit version/auth/catalog/value/cancel results for named services; compatibility is not a new native-engine claim |

Managed-service adapters require disposable cloud test projects/accounts and explicit cost budgets. Emulators/mocks alone do not establish production authentication, cancellation or billing behavior. Missing access leaves that adapter unverified; it does not justify claiming support.

The defined broad target includes the current eight products plus MongoDB, Redis, Valkey, the five warehouse/query products above, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, DynamoDB, Cassandra/ScyllaDB, Db2, Neo4j and the three vector stores: **26 named database products**. PostgreSQL vector capabilities can use the existing SQL path earlier. Other engines, client importers and advanced vendor management APIs are expansion work after this defined target; do not silently turn “all databases” into an unbounded completion condition.

## Final hardening and release work

These PR themes recur at release checkpoints; they are not postponed until every adapter exists.

| PR | Scope | Required evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P51 | Security/failure/platform hardening and strict deployment profile | Fuzz parsers/protocol/state boundaries; hostile oversized inputs; cross-principal/instance isolation; TLS/auth failures; interrupted jobs; no orphan work; macOS/Linux/Windows supported-platform matrix. Strong credential isolation is tested with the agent outside the credential runtime's filesystem/process access |
| P52 | Controlled complete performance and task-success report | Commit/versions/data/query/policy/concurrency/TLS; raw samples; p50/p95, throughput, peak RSS/CPU; total installed/download size; cancellation; schema/tool bytes; analyst/pipeline correctness. Keep tables/captures in PR descriptions, not research directories |
| P53 | Product docs, README/site and authentic client workflows | Direct-first setup, optional importers, tested capability matrix, migration notes, troubleshooting; actual Claude/Codex/OpenCode flows and `/mcp` multiple-instance screenshots. Update existing product documentation rather than generating redundant plan pages |
| P54 | Manual npm/native release and installed-package verification | Exact tested commit/version, licenses/SBOM and platform checksums/signatures, registry npx/native/curl smoke tests, safe upgrades/pins/rollback, release notes and update notice. Publishing remains outside CI |

## Dependency and scheduling rules

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[P01-P05 hardening/setup] --> RA[Release A]
  A --> B[P06-P13 native contracts + PostgreSQL]
  B --> C[P14-P21 adapters/import/distribution]
  C --> Cut[P22 cutover + deletion]
  Cut --> RB[Release B]
  B --> N[P23-P24 native non-SQL]
  B --> An[P25-P31 analytical context + memory]
  An --> J[P32-P35 jobs + pipelines]
  N --> RC[Release C]
  J --> RC
  B --> W[P36-P50 broader engines]
  W --> RD[Release D]
  RC --> Final[P51-P54 final acceptance]
  RD --> Final
```

Only independent work overlaps. Metadata/auth/runtime changes run the affected shared conformance matrix. Adapter-only PRs run their engine fixtures plus shared contracts; release checkpoints run the full advertised matrix. This is dependency planning, not an instruction to create parallel agents or all PR branches now.

## Common PR acceptance template

Each implementation PR description must contain the following compact review information:

| Section | Required content |
|---|---|
| Outcome | Concrete trigger and resulting behavior; relevant issue/planned PR ID |
| Scope | Changed capabilities and explicit unsupported/permission-dependent behavior |
| Validation | Table of runtime/engine/platform checks with actual result and relevant denial/failure fixtures |
| Security | Relevant trust/scope changes and demonstrated enforcement; no generic boilerplate checklist |
| Performance/size | Before/after numbers only when measured; app/driver/runtime costs separated |
| Evidence | Real screenshot/recording where useful; raw measurements linked or attached; no invented UI |
| Migration/removal | Compatibility/rollback, actual added and deleted maintained lines, generated/binary changes separately, production dependencies before/after, and replaced paths removed at cutover |

Merge the exact tested head only after applicable required CI is green. A passing happy-path query is insufficient evidence for a new adapter. Do not open empty PRs, close implementation issues because a plan exists, or claim all-engine support from one prototype. Split PRs by reviewable behavior, not a target LOC number.

## Deletion and dependency-removal gates

The roadmap/experiment update itself has **zero net source or manifest changes against main**. The current server has **45 tracked TypeScript source files / 11,427 physical lines** (including declarations, comments and blanks), plus the existing Rust SQL-policy module. This is a replacement baseline, not a promise to delete every TypeScript file or to shrink total LOC while adding the full feature set.

| Component | Already removed | Remaining removal / retention gate |
|---|---|---|
| JavaScript SQL parser | `node-sql-parser` removed in the existing Rust/WASM policy migration | Reuse the Rust policy implementation; remove superseded execution-time checks only after equivalent enforcement is proved |
| Old test/build plumbing | `vitest`, `@vitest/coverage-v8` and `rimraf` removed during Bun migration | Retain tools still used by fixtures, the website or package development |
| TypeScript execution server | No native-server cutover yet | P22 deletes superseded server, pools, adapters, catalog/result execution and obsolete configuration glue after P11–P21 parity; retain only justified launcher, tooling and independent fixtures |
| WASM distribution | Still required by today's JavaScript server | P22 removes generated WASM/bindings from native package payload when no consumer remains; retain/link Rust policy source and required license notices |
| Runtime requirement | Current package still runs JavaScript | Native server must run without Node/Bun; `npx` bootstrap still needs npm/Node, and website/development tooling may use Bun |

All **nine current direct JavaScript production dependencies** have a planned exit from the native server's production dependency closure:

| Current dependency | Replacement work | Removal gate |
|---|---|---|
| `@clack/prompts` | Native guided CLI (P07/P21) | Setup/client/update flows verified |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` | Rust MCP transport/server (P07) | Client/protocol parity; SDK may remain development-only for independent interoperability tests |
| `pg`, `pg-cursor` | Native PostgreSQL adapter (P11) | Exact values, bounded reads, cancellation and existing capabilities preserved |
| `mysql2` | Native MySQL/MariaDB adapter (P14) | Both engines pass advertised contracts |
| `mssql` | Native SQL Server adapter (P15) | Existing auth/types/TLS/cancellation contracts verified |
| `oracledb` | Native Oracle adapter (P16) | LOB/types/auth/cancellation/platform support verified; disclose external client requirements |
| `ssh2` | Native SSH/auth transport (P10) | Host verification, tunneling, cleanup and supported auth paths verified |
| `xml2js` | Native DBeaver importer (P20) | Imported settings/permissions and error privacy verified |

P22 removes these from production installation; move a dependency to development-only **only if an independent integration fixture still uses it**. Rust drivers and their transitive Cargo/native dependencies replace functionality, so this is not a zero-dependency claim. Remove unused `@types/*`, scripts and configuration only after checking remaining consumers. Keep required third-party notices.

Every migration PR reports actual added/deleted maintained source lines, generated/binary changes separately, direct production dependencies before/after, and applicable installed-size measurements. P22 must demonstrate that old execution paths and unused dependencies are absent from the shipped package. Final net LOC and size are measured after native parity; the small PostgreSQL prototype does not establish the complete server's size.

## Code and size budget

| Scope | Rough maintained production LOC |
|---|---:|
| Native server preserving current coverage | 12k–20k Rust |
| Defined broad target with analytics, memory and workflows | 30k–50k Rust total |
| Separate tests, integration fixtures and release tooling for full scope | 20k–40k |

These are estimates excluding dependencies/generated code, assuming maintained drivers and analytical libraries. Rust replaces existing code, so this is not all additional code. More advanced per-engine diagnostics/CDC can expand the estimate. Code clarity, contracts and reuse matter more than minimizing line count. Do not promise the full application will match the prototype's binary size; measure it at each release checkpoint.

## Explicit boundaries

| Boundary | Rule |
|---|---|
| Local filesystem access | Private files alone do not hide credentials from an unrestricted same-user coding agent. The strong isolation claim requires a protected runtime/deployment profile |
| Sensitive database data | Authorized queries can expose sensitive stored values or engine facts. Use grants, views/RLS or approved parameterized queries; output masking is not an inference boundary |
| Memory | Database text and agent notes are untrusted data. They cannot grant access, change policies or become executable instructions automatically |
| Cross-database analysis | Separate scoped calls or explicitly authorized extracted datasets; no implied distributed transactions or automatic data federation |
| Actual query plans | EXPLAIN ANALYZE/actual plans can execute queries and require execution permissions/budgets |
| Pipeline guarantees | Native atomicity where available; explicit idempotence/checkpoints across systems; no blanket exactly-once promise |
| Remote HTTP/team hosting | Optional follow-up with proper authentication and principal/session isolation; not required for the defined stdio-first target and not an unauthenticated shortcut to credential isolation |
| More GUI importers | Add through the same provider contract when formats/credential access permit; no requirement to run those GUIs |
| Quality | Tested guarantees and transparent limitations, not a promise of zero bugs or vulnerabilities |

## Completion checklist

- [x] Release A: hardened direct setup and current fixes installed from npm (3.0.0 / #80); standalone cache-refresh fix #81 merged.
- [ ] Release B: native server preserves current capabilities; superseded execution removed.
- [ ] Release C: non-SQL reads, known-answer analysis, scoped memory and recoverable pipelines verified.
- [ ] Release D: all 26 named products meet their advertised capability contracts; compatibility labels are evidenced.
- [ ] Every advertised adapter passes positive, denied, malformed/oversized, deadline, cancellation and cleanup checks as applicable.
- [ ] Privacy applies to metadata, errors, logs, resources, artifacts, memory and jobs.
- [ ] Optional/external dependencies and complete installation costs are disclosed.
- [ ] Authentic client workflows and versioned migration/release notes are complete.
- [ ] Final exact-head CI, manual publish, installed-package smoke tests and update/rollback checks pass.

items.title: Release Train handoff — الحالة الحالية والمهام المتبقية — 2026-09-03
items.body:
# Release Train Handoff — 2026-09-03

هذا الـIssue هو نقطة الاستئناف الرسمية للمحادثات القادمة. الهدف: معرفة ما تم تنفيذه، ما بقي، وما هي بوابات النشر دون إعادة التشخيص من الصفر.

## الحالة العامة

- المستودع: `AMASI-SA/AMASI-SA`
- Production branch: `hotfix/prod-snap-meta-final`
- Git Production SHA المعروف: `1de6118484ac4fe1d0981e230618dbb573d8c58c`
- Live Production حاليًا ما زال على rollback القديم: `c320c293d1359060ae48931f091046a3e274b309`
- لا يوجد Merge/Publish/Republish معتمد للـRelease Train الحالي.
- Emergent gate يبقى مغلقًا حتى يصل تأكيد صريح أن `build-repair automation` تم تعطيله فعليًا لتطبيق `salla-analytics`.
- عند فتح gate لا ننشر المهام منفردة؛ الهدف النهائي: عدة PRs مستقلة → Final Production Source واحد → Release Intent v5 واحد جديد → Fresh Release Guard lease → **Republish واحد فقط** → verify.

---

# المهام المكتملة

## TASK 1 — Qoyod unsent-orders memory bounds

- PR: #1001
- الحالة: Draft / technically ready
- الهدف: منع heavy scans والضغط الذاكري في unsent-orders.
- تم: bounded cursors، single-flight، cache، concurrency ceiling، frontend polling/coalescing.
- لا تعيد تنفيذ نطاق #1001 في مهام أخرى.
- Release Intent الموجود داخل #1001 قديم خاص بهذه المهمة فقط، ولن يُستخدم كـFinal Intent إذا أضيفت بقية مهام Release Train.

## TASK 2 — Runtime Stability / Mongo / Auth

- PR: #1003
- Branch: `hotfix/runtime-stability-mongo-auth`
- Head: `d68e5fb20837ae935aa7755df436c26368e784a3`
- الحالة: Draft / technically ready
- تم:
  - Mongo pool/timeouts bounded.
  - Owner `/api/auth/me` fast-path يقلل DB reads.
  - transient DB failure → 503 وليس fake 401/logout.
  - Legacy Qoyod frozen polling خُفض من 5s إلى 300s.
  - Plan-B polling adaptive.
  - `/api/live` process-only و`/api/ready` Mongo bounded.
  - Auth retry coalescing.
- لا يوجد file overlap مع #1001.

## TASK 3 — Snapchat Spend Reliability

- PR: #1004
- Branch: `codex/snapchat-spend-reliability`
- Head: `a9d31c94db80b57cb558133c39effa64da92f94c`
- الحالة: Draft / technically ready
- تم:
  - per-day coverage diagnostics.
  - 29/30 يبقى fail-closed لكن يكشف اليوم الناقص بدل `لا بيانات` فقط.
  - targeted retry لليوم المفقود فقط.
  - parent/child run proof alignment.
  - V2 financial scheduler writer authority كل 10 دقائق، selected accounts فقط، lease/single-flight.
  - فصل `last_mezan_check_at` عن provider success/value-change/fact timestamps.
  - منع تحويل incomplete Snapchat إلى final `0.00` أو صافي ربح مزيف.
- لا يوجد file overlap مع #1001/#1003.

## TASK 4 — Salla Missing Orders Reliability

- PR: #1005
- Branch: `codex/salla-missing-orders-reliability`
- Head: `c2c19032b052d7eb3af1d78c86ac3d7ab2ed46e3`
- الحالة: Draft / technically ready
- الملفات: فقط
  - `backend/salla_integration/auto_sync.py`
  - `backend/salla_integration/routes.py`
  - `backend/tests/test_salla_order_discovery_reliability.py`
- root causes reproduced:
  1. checkpoint كان يتقدم رغم فشل طلب فردي، فيمكن أن يخرج الطلب من overlap ويضيع.
  2. discovery كان `page=1`, `per_page=60` فقط، فيفقد الطلب 61+.
- تم:
  - bounded pagination.
  - durable tenant-scoped checkpoint + retry ledger.
  - 24–48h read-first gap reconciliation.
  - missing-only recovery؛ existing webhook orders لا تُكتب من جديد.
  - no background `GET /orders/{id}`.
  - fixture: Salla 192 / Mezan 190 → recover exactly 2 → 192/192 دون rewrite للـ190.
- لا يوجد file overlap مع #1001/#1003/#1004.

## TASK 5A — Preparation Duplicate Units Root Cause Diagnosis

- الحالة: **Diagnosis only — مكتمل تشخيص الكود، لا PR**.
- الطلبات الموثقة:
  - `279346733` — PF `PF-20260829-0092`
  - `279383684` — PF `PF-20260829-0085`
- المؤكد على مستوى الكود:
  - `order_items_with_review_snapshot()` يدمج فقط عند exact `order_item_id`، ومصالحة الهوية التجارية تعمل فقط عندما Snapshot ID فارغ.
  - إذا Current line وReview Snapshot يمثلان نفس القطعة لكن لديهما `order_item_id` مختلف وغير فارغ، يمكن أن يدخل Snapshot كسطر جديد.
  - بعدها يصبح لكل تمثيل Ready IDs / allocations / Batch lines / PDF cards مستقلة.
- التصنيف المثبت: التكرار ليس PDF-only؛ وصل إلى physical preparation workflow قبل PDF.
- `buy_as_gift` ليس له branch سببي مثبت في identity/allocation path.
- sender/receiver phone ليس جزءًا من item identity path.
- **مهم:** incident-specific historical cause للطلبين لم يُثبت 100% بعد لأن Stages 3–11 لم تُقرأ بكل IDs الفعلية؛ لذلك لا تدّعِ أن Salla بريئة تاريخيًا أو أن H2/H3 ثبتت للحالتين بعينهما دون قراءة projections.
- المرشحون تاريخيًا: 45 PDF منطقيًا، 19 ملفًا فيها repeated order numbers، 21 order candidates، 40 excess-card candidates؛ هذه ليست Bugs مؤكدة حتى تُقارن بالـauthoritative quantity/options/source identity.

---

# المهمة التالية — TASK 5B

## Preparation Unit Identity Reconciliation

**ابدأ بهذه المهمة قبل TASK 6.**

### المرحلة 5B.0 — Evidence completion read-only

للطلبين `279346733` و`279383684` حاول قراءة فقط:
- `unified_orders.products`
- `raw_by_source.salla_direct.items` إن كانت محفوظة
- `workflow.items`
- review snapshot identity
- allocations
- batch stored lines

واربط المعرفين:
- `02937e4c63aa5fa3a3452bcaf97d610c`
- `87097cf3b19d5be3aec25e5495f02e15`

إذا ثبت Current ID != Snapshot ID مع نفس authoritative commercial identity وquantity=1 → `incident_root_cause_confirmed=true`.
إذا لم تتوفر projections الكافية → لا تخمّن؛ استخدم `code_defect_confirmed=true` و`incident_root_cause_confirmed=false` ثم نفذ الإصلاح الوقائي فقط.

### Root fix المطلوب

- exact `order_item_id` أولًا.
- ثم stable `source_item_id` عندما يكون موثوقًا.
- fallback commercial identity فقط في One-to-One unambiguous case:
  `order_number + product/parent/variant/SKU + canonical options/customization fingerprint`.
- لا dedupe أعمى.
- ambiguity → Fail Closed / keep distinct.
- حافظ على quantity=2 الحقيقية، السطور Provider الحقيقية المتطابقة، ونفس SKU بخيارات/تخصيص مختلف.

### Authoritative quantity guard

# TASK 6 — Products V2 / Salla Publish Reliability

ابدأها **بعد TASK 5B** في Draft PR مستقل.

الصفحة المتأثرة مثالًا:

`/products-v2?missing_mezan_cost=1&sold_only=1&from=2026-09-03&to=2026-09-03&product=mpv2_358058139&focus=cost`

الأعراض المثبتة من UI والكود:

1. Cloudflare origin error: `The origin web server sent a response that Cloudflare could not parse...`.
2. الصفحة قد تعرض تفاصيل منتج محدد بينما القائمة تقول `0 منتج` / لا توجد منتجات ناقصة تكلفة.
3. `product=` يختار المنتج المفتوح، بينما filtered cohort يستخدم مسارًا مختلفًا و`product_ids` عند الحاجة؛ direct cost link قد يعمل full cohort scan بلا داعٍ.
4. فتح المنتج ينفذ `refreshProductV2Details()` مع cost read في `Promise.all`؛ refresh يقرأ Salla live `GET /products/{id}` ثم يكتب Mongo/detail log وقد يحدث cost revision.
5. بالتالي محرر تكلفة ميزان المحلي يعتمد على Salla availability؛ هذا يجب فصله.
6. list path قد ينتظر `syncRecentProductsV2()` قبل العرض.
7. `MezanProductsAutoSync` ينفذ force recent sync كل 60s عندما الصفحة مفتوحة.
8. publish الحالي إلى Salla متزامن طويل: GET current → PUT update → GET verify → وقد يوجد PUT rollback عند verification mismatch.
9. إذا PUT نجح ثم verification timeout، generic failure لا يعني أن التعديل لم يصل؛ نحتاج `publish_outcome=unknown` / reconciliation بدل blind re-PUT.

### Target architecture

- **Local-first product editor:** عرض بيانات Mezan + Cost Profile فورًا، بلا Salla blocking وبلا Mongo write لمجرد فتح الصفحة.
- direct product cost path عند `product=...&focus=cost` بدل full sold cohort scan.
- فصل selected product عن filtered cohort حتى لا يظهر 0 products مع تفاصيل وكأنها ضمن القائمة.
- local Mezan cost save لا يعتمد على Salla.
- Salla refresh يكون background غير مانع أو زر صريح.
- publish state machine واضحة: `preparing → publishing → verifying → succeeded` أو `verification_pending/outcome_unknown/failed/rollback_required`.
- لا blind retry بعد unknown outcome.
- API transient errors يجب أن ترجع JSON منظمًا بدل origin response ناقص/غير قابل للتفسير.
- راجع force-sync كل 60s؛ اجعله non-blocking, single-flight, no overlap with publish، أو أبطأ/event-driven حسب القياس.
- UI يظهر مرحلة النشر الحالية والخطأ المحدد.
- Mezan internal cost fields تبقى protected؛ `salla_cost_price` فقط الحقل التجاري المسموح صراحة للنشر عند الحاجة.

# M15–M17 integration ledger

This issue is the durable integration ledger for the parallel workstreams. Update it with dated, evidence-linked comments as branches, PRs, checks, or staging releases change. The master contract remains [docs/MASTER_ROADMAP_AND_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md](https://github.com/zsoltacsai/wpcaregrid/blob/943deb62558940181b948771b7abdf70e76ae516/docs/MASTER_ROADMAP_AND_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md). This ledger does not change milestone status or authorize customer, staging, production, billing, credential, or infrastructure operations.

## Initial verified snapshot — 2026-10-24 20:31 UTC

- Authoritative branch: `claude/ecstatic-wozniak-oemyuf`
- Primary SHA: `943deb62558940181b948771b7abdf70e76ae516` (PR #173 merge; signed commit verified)
- Exact-SHA CI: [run 40128417134](https://github.com/zsoltacsai/wpcaregrid/actions/runs/40128417134), 37/37 jobs successful; mandatory Server MySQL process-concurrency gate passed.
- Active ruleset: [Authoritative primary release controls](https://github.com/zsoltacsai/wpcaregrid/rules/25300175), active on the authoritative branch. Pull request required, stale approvals dismissed, review threads resolved, strict required status checks; bypass disabled. Required contexts at this snapshot: Quality; Server PHP 8.4 SQLite/MySQL/MariaDB; Connector-in-WordPress PHP 8.4 SQLite/MySQL/MariaDB. Recheck for every candidate and merge.
- Open PRs: none at the time of inspection.
- Staging read-only verification: `stg1.wpcaregrid.com`, application SHA `761e0e5d37558da808ac961ca2d2a68b4ffab0db`, clean worktree, maintenance gate inactive, `/up` returned 200. This is behind the docs-only primary commit; no deployment is needed for PR #173.
- M14 remains `CLOSED — VERIFIED` within its documented scope. This ledger does not reopen it.

## Isolated local workspaces

All four were created clean from the same exact baseline; these branches are local-only and were absent from GitHub at initial inspection.

| Stream | Branch | Workspace suffix | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| M15 pilot and operations | `codex/m15-pilot-readiness` | `.codex-worktrees/m15-pilot-readiness` | Thread 1 |
| M16 frontend and UX | `codex/m16-frontend-ux` | `.codex-worktrees/m16-frontend-ux` | Thread 2 |
| M17 production readiness | `codex/m17-production-readiness` | `.codex-worktrees/m17-production-readiness` | Thread 3 |
| Integration and QA | `codex/integration-qa` | `.codex-worktrees/integration-qa` | Thread 4 |

The shared dirty original checkout was not changed. Do not reset or clean another workspace. Before pushing, refresh primary, confirm the assigned branch still has a single owner, and update the candidate using normal fast-forward/rebase mechanisms; never force-push.

## File fences and integration protocol

- Thread 4 is sole editor for `docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md`, the master evidence index, and integration sequencing.
- Thread 1 owns Connector/polling/inventory/security/backup implementation and its tests; it proposes scoped `docs/PILOT.md` edits for Thread 4 to integrate.
- Thread 2 owns views/components, CSS/JS, public pages, and browser/accessibility tests; no backend authorization, billing, privacy, scanner, backup, or payment policy changes.
- Thread 3 owns production-readiness, threat/ops, monitoring, incident/DR and launch-input evidence; `docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md` edits are proposed for Thread 4 to integrate.
- `docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md`, `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`, and `docs/PILOT.md` have one editor at a time. Migrations/models/shared enums, CI workflow changes, and dependency lockfiles are serialized and assigned by Thread 4.
- Focused PRs target the authoritative branch. Review the entire diff and exact PR-head CI; no mandatory check may be skipped, including the MySQL process-concurrency gate. Merge only through current protection, then verify the exact merge SHA and its full CI.
- Runtime changes are deployed one at a time through the protected staging controller only after exact merge-SHA CI; capture the receipt and verify health. Docs-only changes do not need deployment. No production deployment is authorized.
- Keep M15–M17 proposed until their acceptance matrices are Owner-approved. Begin only safe scoped work within each stream’s boundaries. No live site operation, customer data change, scan/update/restore, secret creation, payment, or infrastructure mutation without its separate documented authorization and gates.
- Use the report template in the master roadmap. Unknown/stale is not pass; CI success is not operational readiness.

## Update format

Each stream should comment with: exact branch/workspace and starting SHA; owned scope/files; focused checks; PR/candidate SHA; exact-head CI and mandatory MySQL concurrency result; review/merge SHA and exact merge CI; staging receipt/deployed SHA or “none”; evidence links; risks/dependencies; next action. Thread 4 reconciles this ledger and current status from evidence.

items.title: Plan: experiments to find the lever after gen 5 (search-mean target, head-vs-search, coverage, PUCT)
items.body:
> **Execution index:** #707 is the active central workstream board (successor to closed #679), including Codex admission, value diagnosis, the fixed audit (#681), diversity, PUCT, and Sol/PT-Sol benchmarking (#355). The active goal is to explain whether PV training improves deployed admission and validate one targeted improvement against production W64. The dated tables below are historical snapshots; use #707 and subsequent result comments for current execution status. No board entry itself grants run or deployment authority.

## Current evidence and remaining goal (reconciled 2026-10-06)

The [measurement corrections](https://github.com/jerryyyu/shengji/issues/663#issuecomment-5899900689) supersede the unsupported ceiling and null-implies-mechanism claims in the original plan. #707 is the execution board; exact lane predeclarations, reviewed artifacts and RELEASE receipts govern runs.

| Question | Evidence now | Still unproven / next gate |
|---|---|---|
| Did trained policy heads improve actual K8 admission? | [Completed DEV read](https://github.com/jerryyyu/shengji/issues/663#issuecomment-5959174014): 180 roots / 60 deals, no missing or failed roots. SMV3 vs historical release30: exclusion-regret delta **−0.002296**, pointwise95% [−0.004680,−0.000314]; reference-best inclusion **+4.44pp**, [1.67,7.22]pp. Equal-deal weighting. | Improvement against a fixed reference evaluator, **not rollout truth**, deployed prevalence, or a causal estimate of extra PV data alone. This is not a new model beating currently served SMV3. |
| Why might admission gains fail to reach gameplay? | [Saved transition census](https://github.com/jerryyyu/shengji/issues/663#issuecomment-5960660166): 121/180 roots have ≤8 legal actions and no pruning opportunity. SMV3 changes membership on50 roots, but33 of those changes leave best admitted reference value unchanged; best reference opportunity improves on14 and worsens on3. | These are unweighted root counts, not deal-level effects. The collector does not contain actual served choices/ties/deadline outcomes. Downstream value selection, ordering and fallback remain hypotheses to isolate—not an established causal diagnosis. |
| Is a targeted improvement validated against production W64? | **Satisfied for the combined search-policy change:** [fresh-ten Combo2 confirmation](https://github.com/jerryyyu/shengji/issues/676#issuecomment-5962364713) **+0.046136 [95% +0.024216,+0.068056]**, health/provenance PASS; both policies compared against common MC-LCB. | Pooled twenty descriptive only; no component attribution, direct H2H or causal training-data claim. No further extension; archive and any deployment/release remain separate. C11 training is not yet a strength result. |
| Is the aligned Sol/PT-Sol benchmark complete? | **Incomplete; recovery r3 failed terminal admission on an illegal model-requested rollout.** [#355](https://github.com/jerryyyu/shengji/issues/355) retains the saved scientific snapshot: 3/9 policies complete, M1+prior partial, 5/9 unstarted; no new accepted panel readout. Historical 151-complete/1-failed/208-unattempted counts are not current attempt totals. | Complete retained-lineage/cost and failure-evidence implementation, review the amended disposition and sensitivity analysis, then obtain Jerry’s separate retry and amendment decisions and Claude RELEASE. [Design review](https://github.com/jerryyyu/shengji/issues/355#issuecomment-6009423982). No retry authority implied; final aligned nine-row/360-round readout remains required. |

Reconciliation of execution pointers and Sol status only; historical scientific estimates retained. — Codex

**Interpretation boundary:** training improved reference-scored admission relative to historical release30 on this DEV panel; the evidence does not support “policy admission never improves.” It also does not establish why a better standalone head can lose as a served package. Keep membership change → available reference-value change → actual played-action change distinct in the next already-planned isolation measurement. No new experiment or launch authority is created by this reconciliation.

---

## Historical status (2026-09-30 02:3x ET; the revised order below supersedes the tiers)

| step | what | status |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | SMV3 sealed; outcome + search-mean heads screened as served vs r30 | **outcome head CONFIRMED** v36a +0.0361 → v36a2 (fresh, predeclared, read of record) **+0.0393 [+0.0033, +0.0752]**; search-mean head v36b −0.0523 [−0.0905, −0.0140], settled negative |
| 0b | policy heads alone vs SmartBot (8k deals) | done: production +0.101, arm A −0.044, arm C +0.097, arm F +0.238, **SMV3 +0.316** |
| 1 | offline actual-K8 admission diagnostic (production / arm F / SMV3) | to design (next) |
| 2 | policy-only gameplay screen, production's value fixed | prerequisite #664 merged; lane to re-scope |
| 3 | counterfactual candidate-value diagnostic, admission fixed | to design |
| 4 | one targeted change + fresh confirmation | gated on 1–3 |
| — | **deploy SMV3 outcome head as release 36** through the standard gate | **Jerry's call** |

Jerry, 2026-09-29: "come up with a list of experiments for us to run given the discussion" / "do we have a GitHub issue with latest plan of runs?". This is that issue. Each tier is gated on the tier before it, so the order is the plan.

## Historical hypotheses (not established diagnoses)

**Original pre-SMV3 premise, superseded as a blanket statement by step0's positive SMV3 outcome-package result:** the record then did not show model scaling working; the earlier strength gains came from the search (shortlist + prior at release 27, pv-search at release 29: +0.086 card play, +0.049 served), and every retrain (v5, gen-1 retrains, the grid trunk in play, gen-4, gen-5 arms A–F over 176k→496k deals) read null or negative. Val cross-entropy sat near 0.626 across gen 5. Four candidate mechanisms, each a hypothesis with a direct check:

1. **The ceiling is the teacher, not the model.** Every label but the realised outcome is a fixed teacher's opinion; the pv-search means are a bootstrap of the served head itself (arm B→C: +160k pv deals, null).
2. **The data covers the wrong states.** Exploration changes the played action 0.2% of the time; the search queries the value net on the counterfactual candidates the teacher never played.
3. **The realised-outcome label is noise at the margin.** One 204-class draw per afterstate; candidate margins ~0.02 half-levels vs label noise ~0.5; early stop at epoch 8 on 55M rows.
4. **The screen cannot see the effect scaling would plausibly give** (MDE80 ≈ 0.05 vs a few hundredths expected).

Plus two recipe habits: selection on cross-entropy (calibration) while the search consumes ranking; warm-start-and-stop-early on the same data, which is fine-tuning, not a scaling run.

The loop is broken in two places: the value head never trains on the search's better estimate (it trains on the realised outcome), and the policy head, though distilled from search, only gates admission (anchor + top-7) with no tree for a better prior to steer. **Correction:** the historical4.6% figure is miss_at_64 for the recorded played action, stratified equally; it is not deployed anchor-plus-top-7 reference-best recall and does not bound deal-level strength gain. See the measurement corrections above.

## Tier 1 — cheap and decisive (this week)

| # | experiment | answers | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **SMV3 two-head screens.** `GEN5-PROD-SOFT-allPV-plusMCLCB-496k-SMV3` (arm F's recipe, sidecar v3 #658: the search-mean head trains on all 496k shards). Export the OUTCOME head → v36a on Perf (seeds 31960910..32360910) and the SEARCH-MEAN head → v36b on cloud (32460910..32860910), each as served vs release 30. | does training the value head on the search's own estimate (played action only) move the served read | training, epoch 14, best val_ce 0.6205; after-seal waiter armed; lanes dry-run clean on tree 9ec54528 |
| 2 | **Head-vs-head under the same search.** pv-search with the JS-M1 head (it has a policy head) vs pv-search with the production soft head, same recipe, same windows. | how much of release 29's gain was the model vs the search; whether value-head accuracy is the binding constraint at all | to write |
| 3 | **Off-trajectory value error (diagnostic).** On ~2k real decisions, the value net's error on the played afterstate vs the unplayed candidates, ground truth = long rollouts or the exact endgame solver. | mechanism 2 directly: is the net systematically worse on the branches the search compares | to write; cloud, hours |

## Tier 2 — one retrain each, gated on tier 1

| # | experiment | run if |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | **All-candidate search-mean target.** Value head trained on the search's 64-world mean over EVERY admitted candidate, not only the played one (the full AlphaZero move). | #1's search-mean export reads at or above the outcome export |
| 5 | **Select on ranking, not calibration.** Same recipe, checkpoint chosen by rank regret against rollout truth instead of val_ce; reuses the cached candidate sets. | always cheap; run alongside #4 |
| 6 | **From-scratch scaling run with a real schedule.** No warm start, LR schedule sized to 55M rows, batch 4096 with scaled LR, 20 epochs, no early stop. | #2 says the head matters |

## Tier 3 — data generation for coverage, gated on #3

| # | experiment |
|---|---|
| 7 | **Real exploration**: a store where exploration changes the played action on 5–10% of decisions, so counterfactual branches enter the corpus; head trained with it added vs arm C's recipe. |
| 8 | **Mixed-strength seats**: heuristic/SmartBot at some positions so outcomes vary and the net sees losing lines. |
| 9 | **Independent teacher labels**: runSL1..4 (shortlist rollout means from a teacher that is not the head being trained; #436). runSL1/2 sealed 09-29 08:1x ET, runSL3/4 seal ~21:00 ET. One-variable retrain adding the four stores vs arm C. |

## Tier 4 — search structure (the larger bet)

| # | experiment |
|---|---|
| 10 | **PUCT over the admitted set** (#436): give the policy prior influence over allocation after admission. This is a mechanism hypothesis; the former4.6% ceiling rationale is invalid. |
| 11 | **Wider admission as a control**: K=12 vs K=8 with the same head. A narrow, adequately powered equivalence result would constrain a specified effect; an interval crossing zero alone does not show admission is non-limiting. |

## Historical decision rules — superseded, not executable gates

The following original implications are retained as history, **not valid causal deductions or current run instructions**. Nulls do not identify a mechanism or justify stopping a research line. Current lane-specific predeclarations and the measurement corrections above supersede these rules, including the blanket outcome-dependent extension rule and obsolete release30 control.


- #1 search-mean ≥ outcome → run #4 and #5. #1 both null → the played-action target was too small a change; #4 is still the next run, #6 only if #2 says the head matters.
- #2 old head ≈ new head → stop retraining on this corpus for strength; spend compute on #3, #7–9 and #10.
- #3 off-trajectory error ≫ on-trajectory → #7 and #8 before any further retrain.

Every screen: five 520-cluster windows vs release 30, common MC-LCB control, fresh seeds registered before dealing; extend to ten only if the point clears +0.015 (five-window triage). Say "inconclusive" when the interval spans zero.

— Claude

items.title: After current experiments, prioritize integrated token-efficiency evaluation
items.body:
## Three-arm fixed-task and temporary-obstruction evidence (2026-11-01)

The earlier statements below that no third arm exists are superseded **for these fixed scripted Calc workloads only**. [Two opposite-order fixed-task blocks](https://github.com/Unjuno/agent-interface/tree/main/research/integration/wslc_calc_three_arm_reverse_20261101) and [two opposite-order temporary-obstruction blocks](https://github.com/Unjuno/agent-interface/tree/main/research/integration/wslc_calc_three_arm_obstruction_reverse_20261101) compare direct guarded execution, compiled continuation and fresh regrounding. All twelve attempts independently scored exact 472/615 and recorded verified release and neutral final X input. In the temporary-obstruction blocks the caller detected test-injected changed pixels before its recorded mint/program, and the test removed its own overlay before a new model grounding; this is not a runtime stale-handle refusal.

For the fixed task, direct / compiled / fresh task medians were 6.258 / 6.561 / 9.659 s. With temporary obstruction they were 9.278 / 10.150 / 12.096 s. Each median has two samples; cached input is included in token totals. Candidates, captures, accounting, releases and saved files are preserved and both comparison auditors re-run the block audits. The earlier exploratory direct baseline includes a failed setup and an incorrectly inherited pass condition; it is retained separately and is not silently counted in these blocks.

These are fixed-value expected-OCR, scripted-Save workloads with different cache/provider conditions and route internals, unequal model calls, excluded startup/preparation/audit in the task interval, and small sample counts. They do not settle general speed, cost or reliability, persistent-obstruction or partial-input recovery, arbitrary edits, or MAP01. Cold/warm/invalidation/repair across broader workloads and complete lifecycle/all-attempt accounting remain open. Keep this issue open.
